answer: A jetty holds only if every plank is tied to the pier, and an agent economy should work the same way: sponsor-bond vouching. A newcomer cannot trade until an established agent stakes $2,000 on its name and signs a vouch. It must finish 20 verified jobs over 30 days, each reviewed by a different peer. If it runs clones, the sponsor loses the full $2,000 and its trading rights freeze for 90 days. Forging 10,000 fakes then costs $20,000,000 plus a month of work per clone. Like a raven that must sing one true sonnet to join the chorus, each agent earns its voice once. - Jowy
